MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  MARCH 13, 2019

  A regular meeting of the General Plan Advisory Committee (GPAC) of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive
  North, by CHAIR SCHMITZ.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Schmitz, Zuckerman, Addleman, Arata, Bayer,
  Carman, Carrese, Corman, Shinn

  Committee Members Absent:  Buresh, Friedman, Medawar, Portugal, Seamans, Silvano,
  Stegura

  Student Members Present:  Michael Scandialato

  Staff Members Present:  Assistant City Manager Grammer, Sr. Planner Naughton,
  Associate Planner Thom, Administrative Assistant Corea

  Also Present:  Rajeev Bhatia, Dyett & Bhatia
  Meghan McNulty, Dyett & Bhatia

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  JANUARY 29, 2019.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER
  to,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE GPAC MEETING OF JANUARY 29, 2019 AS
  PRESENTED.

  AYES:  Chair Schmitz, Zuckerman, Addleman, Arata, Bayer, Carman, Carrese, Shinn
  NOES:
  ABSENT: Buresh, Friedman, Medawar, Portugal, Seamans, Silvano, Stegura
  ABSTAIN: Corman

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATION NOT ON AGENDA

  NONE

  5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  AGENDA OVERVIEW/RECAP OF LAST MEETING

  Rajeev Bhatia, Dyett & Bhatia provided a recap of the last meeting and goals for future meetings.

  Meghan McNulty, Dyett & Bhatia provided an overview of the changes to the Vision & Guiding
  Principles and Goals which is included in Workbook #2.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ asked for input on any items that should be revisited.

  A discussion ensued on the Guiding Principles and the following change was agreed upon by the
  Committee:

  •  Guiding Principles #3 - Remove the term “mixed-use” in the title and change the title to,
  “Promote a central district with a variety of uses”.

  In response to a question by the Committee Members, Mr. Bhatia clarified that the Guiding
  Principles are not numbered in the order of priority.

  The Committee discussed the section on goals.

General Plan Advisory Committee  1
Meeting Minutes, March 13, 2019
   •  Goal #3 – Change the beginning to “Promote a socially vibrant, active, central district with
  mixed uses…”

  •  Goal #5 – Change to “Protect health and safety by working to ensure that the former Palos
  Verdes Landfill remains an undeveloped space limited to equestrian and passive  uses.”

  •  Goal #7 – Change “… provide the necessary public services and infrastructure” to
  “…provide the necessary services.

  •  Add a Goal #8 to include maintaining public works (services) and infrastructure.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ left the meeting at 6:45 p.m. and COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN chaired
  the remainder of the meeting.
  B.  LAND USE AND COMMUNITY DESIGN ELEMENT WORKBOOK #2
  The GPAC held a general discussion, which included the following:

  •  Committee Members suggested that no housing should be allowed on the Promenade on the
  Peninsula site.
  o Staff expressed concern that this may be spot zoning.
  o Disallowing housing may remove a human element from the commercial district.

  •  In response to a question regarding the states ADU requirements, Staff commented that it is
  not likely that the City can meet Regional Housing Needs Allocations (RHNA) goals through
  ADUs alone.

  •  There was a consensus among the Committee Members that housing should not be allowed
  outside of the hatched area shown on the map (included on pg.8 of Workbook #2). Staff added
  that housing requires a CUP in the Commercial General Zone.

  •  Staff commented that it is important to leave flexibility in the district since this is a long-term
  document.

  •  In response to a question by the COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Sr. Planner Naughton
  stated that unless the community wants to look at residential areas, then the only place to look
  at providing additional housing is in the commercial corridor in order to meet housing
  requirements.

  •  Mr. Bhatia discussed that the city may need to look beyond the Mixed Use District to meet
  the RHNA and that the State is increasingly looking at implementing objective standards.

  •  There was a consensus among COMMITTEE MEMBERS to continue this discussion at a
  future meeting.
  6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

  NONE

  7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  •  Add the following question: “If limited additional housing opportunities are provided, where
  would they be located.”
  •  Discuss if the Mixed-Use Overlay boundary should be amended.
  •  Acreage totals for parcels.
  •  Discuss how housing could be addressed to meet State requirements.
  •  Discussion on Neighborhood Compatibility.
  •  Discussion on the Commercial District.

  8.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 8:10 p.m.
